articles.title: Turkish officials 'destroyed' pro-opposition TV channel, owner tells BBC
articles.description: The headquarters of Halk TV were raided last month, the latest in a series of crackdowns on news sources deemed critical of the government.

articles.title: Eight killed in Peruvian military helicopter crash
articles.description: The pilot was the sole survivor of the crash during a rescue mission in a remote area known for drug trafficking.

articles.title: 'Poison seller' Kenneth Law apologises in court to the families of his victims
articles.description: The Canadian man, who pleaded guilty to 14 counts of aiding and abetting suicide earlier this year, said he was remorseful for his actions.

articles.title: Behind China's spectacular rise, voices who defied it say they are being drowned out
articles.description: China's immense clout now also has the flex of soft power. Critics and dissidents say their voices are being drowned out.

articles.title: A clinic is reassessing people with ADHD and autism diagnoses - but critics fear it could deepen stigma
articles.description: While many people find a diagnosis for ADHD or autism affirming, a government-funded clinic in Sweden is re-assessing people who feel it does not reflect them.

articles.title: The Indian 'Tamasha queen' whose fans paid for a show that never happened
articles.description: A new Bollywood flim spotlights the remarkable life of dancer and singer Vithabhai Narayangaonkar.

articles.title: Nigeria's 'ultimate hard man' who become an online meme
articles.description: Before becoming a household name in the Nigerian film industry, Edochie built a career in broadcasting.

articles.description:

articles.title: Australia’s east coast deluged by storms as roads flood and damaging winds forecast for NSW and Victoria
articles.description:
Severe weather and flood watch warnings are in place as a storm band moves from central Queensland through NSW to Victoria and Tasmania

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The final weekend of Australia’s wettest spring on record for an El Niño year is delivering a deluge of storms and heavy rain.

Severe weather and flood watch warnings are in place across the eastern states as a weather band moves from central Queensland through New South Wales to Victoria and Tasmania.

Continue reading...

articles.title: La succession: France’s wealthiest family said to be battling over who will take over LVMH
articles.description:
Bernard Arnault’s children – described as ‘modern-day French royals’ – are subject of rivalry rumours over who will succeed him

They are France’s richest family, leading the world’s biggest luxury goods empire, dressed in matching Dior suits – a clan so powerful they have been described as modern-day French royals.

But in recent months, the family dynasty of Bernard Arnault, 77, the billionaire head of the LVMH group whose brands range from Louis Vuitton handbags to Tiffany jewellery, has become the subject of speculation about internal rivalry over which of his children could take over the company.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Yuri and I used to play football together. Then I spotted his name among Russia’s war dead
articles.description:
I had no idea he had gone to fight in Ukraine and without hacked data I would probably never have learned of his death

One evening, after weeks spent counting Russia’s war dead, I began looking for names I might recognise.

My colleagues and I had been working our way through more than 11m death certificates leaked from Rosstat, Russia’s state statistics agency, and identifying nearly half a million Russian soldiers who had died in the war in Ukraine.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Schools in England must set aside time for pupils to read for pleasure
articles.description:
Education secretary expected to announce measures as part of proposed reforms to national curriculum

Schools in England will have to allocate time for children to read for pleasure as part of Labour’s proposed reforms of the national curriculum.

The education secretary, Lucy Powell, is expected to announce to parliament on Monday that primary schools must earmark time each day for children to read.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Charity set up by Captain Tom Moore’s family applies to be struck off
articles.description:
Watchdog had found ‘repeated’ misconduct by veteran’s daughter and her husband in running the foundation

A charity set up by the family of the pandemic fundraiser Captain Sir Tom Moore has applied to be struck off.

The charity is now known as the 1189808 Foundation, having dropped Moore’s name at the request of his family last year.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Purse found of woman, 24, swept from California beach three weeks ago
articles.description:
Se Nah Park was overwhelmed by a wave at the notorious Panther Beach

The purse of a 24-year-old who was swept into the ocean at a notorious California beach three weeks ago was found on Wednesday, as the west coast saw record high king tides.

The Santa Cruz county sheriff’s office confirmed that Se Nah Park’s purse was found by a beachgoer at 4 Mile Beach, south of Panther Beach, where she was swept away into the ocean on 8 November.

Continue reading...

articles.title: OpenAI countersues Apple for allegedly stealing trade secrets
articles.description:
Lawsuit also alleging pressure on hardware suppliers comes after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching employees

OpenAI sued Apple on Friday, accusing the company of stealing its trade secrets and discouraging hardware suppliers from working on future OpenAI devices.

The suit, filed in northern California federal court, comes after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching its employees to gain access to its technology.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Israeli strike kills two Doctors Without Borders staff in Gaza
articles.description: Two staff members of Doctors Without Borders in Gaza were killed by an Israeli strike. The Israeli army identified them as Hamas members, while MSF condemned the attack.

articles.title: US military says cyber systems secure after reports of Air Force hack
articles.description: The US military has dismissed concerns about its cybersecurity after reports of a potential hack on the Air Force’s cloud system. A Defense Department official did not specifically deny the breach but assured systems are secure.

articles.title: Von Dellingshausen in charge at Australian PGA Championship as Noren lurks
articles.description: Nicolai von Dellingshausen leads the Australian PGA Championship with a three-shot advantage, while Alex Noren remains a close contender.

articles.title: Warriors’ Curry ‘making good progress’ after oblique injury
articles.description: Stephen Curry is making progress in recovering from an oblique abdominal tear but will miss at least three more games.

articles.title: Messi’s defending champions Miami knocked out of MLS Cup playoffs
articles.description: Columbus Crew defeated Inter Miami 1-0, eliminating them from the MLS Cup playoffs. Santiago Rodriguez scored the decisive goal in injury time.

articles.title: Saudi military industries chief wraps up UK visit focused on defense tech transfer, investment
articles.description: Bandar Alkhorayef, acting governor of Saudi Arabia’s General Authority for Military Industries, has concluded a visit to the UK aimed at enhancing defense-industrial collaboration and attracting investments into Saudi Arabia's military manufacturing sector. During his meetings, discussions centered on technology transfer and strengthening national defense capabilities, aligning with the Kingdom's Vision 2030 goal to localize over 50% of military spending.

articles.title: Syrian governors mark second anniversary of uprising that toppled Assad regime
articles.description: On the second anniversary of the Deterrence of Aggression Battle, Syrian governors commemorated the military campaign that led to the ousting of Bashar Assad's regime. They emphasized the importance of safeguarding liberation gains, initiating reforms, and facilitating the return of displaced Syrians while honoring the sacrifices made during the uprising against decades of Assad family rule.

articles.title: Jermaine Haley, known as WWE wrestler Bronson Reed, dies at 38
articles.description: Jermaine Haley, also known as WWE wrestler Bronson Reed, passed away at 38 due to medical complications. WWE announced his death without detailing the cause.

articles.title: 14 found dead on migrant boat off Spain’s Canary Islands
articles.description: Fourteen migrants tragically died when a boat carrying about 100 people was rescued near Spain's Canary Islands, highlighting the perilous nature of this migration route. The incident comes amidst a surge in migrant arrivals, with record numbers reaching the islands, raising urgent calls for action from local leaders and intensified debates on immigration policy ahead of Spain's general election.

articles.title: Syria outlines efforts to tackle Assad chemical weapons legacy at OPCW meeting in The Hague
articles.description: At the OPCW meeting in The Hague, a Syrian delegation highlighted efforts to address the legacy of the previous regime's chemical weapons, seeking international support for mine clearance and post-conflict recovery. Led by Minister Raed Al-Saleh, the delegation engaged in discussions to enhance cooperation on victim support, infrastructure rehabilitation, and the safe return of displaced Syrians, while emphasizing the need for a roadmap to complete the destruction of chemical weapons.

articles.title: Iraq oil smuggling clampdown threatens ties with Kurds, Iran
articles.description: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi's crackdown on oil smuggling is garnering praise from the US but risks straining relations with Iraq's Kurds and Iran. By aiming to centralize control over oil resources and border crossings, Zaidi seeks to assert state authority and combat corruption, which the US supports in its effort to counter Iran's influence and secure investments in Iraq. However, this move has sparked tensions with Kurdish authorities, who fear a threat to their autonomy.

articles.title: Syria security forces suffer four deaths in separate attacks in Deir Ezzor, Daraa
articles.description: DAMASCUS: Four Syrian security and military personnel were killed in separate attacks in Deir Ezzor and Daraa provinces, according to reports by the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA), highlighting continuing security challenges facing the country. Two Internal Security personnel were killed and another wounded on Friday when gunmen attacked a security patrol in the city of Deir Ezzor, SANA reported, citing the Internal Security Forces. In a separate incident, two Syrian Arab Army soldiers were k

articles.title: Italy taken to decider again in Davis Cup semifinal
articles.description: Italy faces a deciding doubles match in the Davis Cup semifinal after the Czech Republic tied the series at 1-1. A win is crucial for Italy’s hopes of securing a fourth consecutive title.

articles.title: UK’s Princess Catherine fights back tears over children’s cancer support
articles.description: LONDON: Britain’s Princess Catherine is seen brushing away tears in a new documentary about her cancer journey as she listens to messages of support from her three children. Catherine, 44, who is married to heir to the throne Prince William, was filmed for the highly personal documentary taking part in one of the UK’s best-known endurance events, the Three Peaks Challenge. Participants in the challenge, which the princess completed in June, climb the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wa

articles.title: OpenAI countersues Apple in row over trade secrets, suppliers
articles.description: SAN FRANCISCO: OpenAI countersued Apple on Friday, alleging that the iPhone maker committed similar trade secret theft that it had accused the ChatGPT provider of this summer. OpenAI alleged that Apple was stealing trade secrets through a former employee and pressuring shared suppliers to hamper its entry into the connected devices market. The countersuit came in a filing Friday in federal court in San Jose, California, in which OpenAI responded to a lawsuit filed by Apple on July 10 against it

articles.title: Parts of the US clean up, power being restored after Thanksgiving storm soaks East Coast
articles.description: The aftermath of a Thanksgiving storm has led to cleanup efforts and gradual restoration of power across the East Coast, impacting areas from New York to Virginia.

articles.title: Army deems lead azide detonation a success but criticism lingers over notification
articles.description: The US Army’s detonation of old lead azide stockpiles is considered successful. However, concerns remain about the transparency and timing of the communication with affected communities.

articles.title: French far-right leader Le Pen clashes with Macron over EU budget
articles.description: BRUSSELS, Belgium: French President Emmanuel Macron slapped down far-right leader Marine Le Pen on Thursday, accusing her of “arrogance” for criticizing a push to lock in the EU’s next budget before France’s 2027 elections. A Brussels summit failed to bridge deep divides over the bloc’s 2028-2034 budget, wrapping up on a sour note after more than 12 hours of talks, with leaders agreeing only that a deal by year-end will be an uphill battle. “We are not there yet,” German Chancellor Friedrich Mer

articles.title: Chelsea suffer third successive loss as Gibbs-White grabs double for Nottingham Forest
articles.description: Chelsea experienced their third consecutive Premier League defeat with Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White playing a pivotal role by scoring twice. The match ended in a 3-2 victory for Forest at City Ground.

articles.title: Where science meets enterprise: Saudi startups transform research into real-world impact
articles.description: Saudi Arabia is heavily investing in water and food research, with startups increasingly commercializing scientific discoveries, raising $1.4 billion in funding and generating $1.1 billion in revenue. Supported by King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), these ventures are developing solutions to local resource challenges, exemplified by products like Plantiva, which aims to enhance agricultural efficiency. The integration of AI is seen as a key factor in accelerating the transition from research to market-ready solutions, crucial for addressing the region's unique environmental challenges.

articles.title: Siddique leads Sharjah Warriorz to first ILT20 win with seven-wicket victory over Dubai Capitals
articles.description: SHARJAH: Junaid Siddique took three wickets before Tim Seifert and Paul Walter led a blistering batting display as Sharjah Warriorz secured their first win of DP World ILT20 Season 5 with a seven-wicket victory over Dubai Capitals on Friday. Siddique finished with figures of 3-25 as the Capitals were bowled out for 126 at Sharjah Cricket Stadium. articles.title: Kuwait summons Iran ambassador over ‘continued Iranian attacks’
articles.description: Kuwait’s foreign ministry summoned Iran’s ambassador in response to ongoing attacks, including a recent drone strike that resulted in fatalities.

articles.title: Rennes fire coach Haise after torrid run
articles.description: RENNES, France: Franck Haise has been sacked by Rennes after a run of five games without a win in all competitions, a source told AFP on Friday. The final straw was Thursday’s 3-1 Europa League defeat at NEC Nijmegen. Frenchman Haise took over in February before helping the Bretons into Europe, and even taking them to the top of Ligue 1 a month ago. Two defeats and a draw in the league coupled with a single point from two games in the Europa League eventually cost the 55-year-old his job. H

articles.title: 27 displaced Syrian families return home to restored Damascus homes
articles.description: DAMASCUS: Twenty-seven Syrian families have returned to their homes in Damascus and the surrounding countryside after years of being displaced because of the civil war, the Syrian Arab News Agency reported on Friday. The families returned to the neighborhoods of Al-Tadamon and Al-Hajar Al-Aswad from the Deir Ballout and Al-Muhammadiya displacement camps in northern Syria under an initiative called Damascus’ Loyalty to Our People in the Camps. articles.title: Saudi falcon festival returns with hefty prize pool
articles.description: RIYADH: The falcon beauty competition rounds commenced on Thursday at the 2026 King Abdulaziz Falconry Festival, the world’s largest gathering of falcons. Running until Monday, the festival features a four-day beauty contest. Each round offers a total prize pool of SR625,000 ($167,000), distributed as SR300,000 for first place, SR175,000 for second, SR100,000 for third, SR30,000 for fourth, and SR20,000 for fifth, underscoring the competition’s prominence within the festival’s program. articles.title: Prosecutors seek 25-year sentence for Canada suicide poison seller
articles.description: MONTREAL: Canadian prosecutors on Friday requested a 25-year prison sentence for a man who sold poison to help people commit suicide, stressing his victims were largely young and experiencing mental distress. Former chef Kenneth Law pleaded guilty earlier this year to aiding 14 suicides in Canada, but he has admitted to selling his so-called suicide kits globally through a series of online forums. Prosecutors had also charged him with murder but, citing a lack of evidence, agreed to withdraw

articles.title: A cheaper route to scaling up carbon capture
articles.description: Governments and companies are moving from climate promises to practical plans. Nearly every major strategy to decarbonize heavy industry now relies on carbon capture, an industrial process that traps carbon dioxide before it escapes into the atmosphere and stores it underground. Industries such as steel, cement, chemicals and gas processing cannot easily avoid producing carbon dioxide, making capture at the source one of the few practical options. articles.title: Paraguay ex-minister arrested in latest bank failure fallout
articles.description: Former Paraguay economy minister Carlos Fernandez Valdovinos has been arrested after turning himself in, related to the collapse of a major bank. Several ex-officials have been detained following the crisis.

articles.title: Canada’s top court upholds Quebec law banning religious symbols in test of unity
articles.description: OTTAWA: Canada’s Supreme Court on Friday upheld Quebec’s ban on religious symbols for public servants, prompting rights groups to warn the ruling unfairly targets Muslim women and weakens legal protections for fundamental rights. The decision is a political win for Quebec’s sovereigntist government and could complicate Prime Minister Mark Carney’s efforts to unify Canada as the country faces a trade war and annexation threats from US President Donald Trump. Quebec’s previous government passed

articles.title: Late En-Nesyri winner keeps Al-Ittihad on heels of SPL leaders
articles.description: ALKHOBAR: After a torrid period before the international break that saw Al-Ittihad drop points to Abha in the league and lose 4-1 to Al-Ain in continental competition, it is safe to say that normality has begun to return for the Tigers. However, how far normality has returned is yet to be determined. Al-Ittihad followed up their 2-0 win against Pakhtakor in the AFC Champions League Elite midweek with a 1-0 victory over one of the season’s surprise packages, Neom. Those three points keep Al-Ittih

articles.title: Can the Lebanese state finally hold Hezbollah to account?
articles.description: Lebanon's Military Court has charged three Hezbollah members with forming armed groups and equipping them with weapons, following the detention of five men in an area with no known Hezbollah presence. This case is part of a larger effort by the Lebanese state to hold Hezbollah accountable for its military activities, challenging the group's longstanding influence amidst growing governmental and public support for anti-corruption and reform measures. The situation raises questions about the state's capacity to enforce its authority without succumbing to Hezbollah's intimidation.

articles.title: Using a drone and a poop-sniffing dog, scientists perform health checks on endangered orcas
articles.description: Scientists are using innovative methods, including drones and a poop-sniffing dog, to assess the health of endangered orcas in the Salish Sea. Despite protections, their population remains at a precarious 76 individuals.

articles.title: Winter Season begins in Asir region
articles.description: RIYADH: Prince Turki bin Talal, the Asir region’s governor and chairman of the Asir Development Authority, has announced the launch of the 2026 Asir Winter Season. The season aims to strengthen Asir’s standing as a global tourism destination distinguished by unique tourism products and year-round events supported by government entities and private-sector partners. Building on the region’s growing tourism momentum, the season highlights Asir’s natural landscapes, culture, arts, and hospitality. I

articles.title: Saudi, UK advocates join forces to tackle gender-based violence
articles.description: Saudi, UK advocates join forces to tackle gender-based violence Lama Alhamawi RIYADH: Marking the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence, UK Ambassador to Saudi Arabia Stephen Hitchen hosted a panel session at his residence in Riyadh, bringing together prominent Saudi leaders in women’s advocacy to spotlight support resources, legal frameworks, and joint efforts to end violence against women and girls. “This event was a reminder of just how much we can learn from one another when we b

articles.title: Thirteen soldiers killed in southwest Niger in attack claimed by Daesh
articles.description: NIAMEY: Thirteen soldiers were killed and 20 wounded in an attack on a National Guard position in southwestern Niger on Thursday, the defense ministry said, while Daesh claimed responsibility on its Telegram channel. The ministry said the attack was carried out by a large group of heavily armed assailants, describing them as terrorists without naming any group. articles.title: 80 culinary experiences converge in heart of historic Riyadh this weekend
articles.description: RIYADH: The Royal Commission for Riyadh City’s “Street Food” weekend event began on Thursday, offering 80 carefully curated culinary experiences in the heart of historic Riyadh, blending authentic local flavors with international tastes. The multi-day event features a packed program of live cooking demonstrations from chefs, tasting sessions, meet-and-greets with chefs, and interactive activities, all set against a winter backdrop. articles.title: UN refugee agency seeks $7.1 billion in 2027
articles.description: GENEVA: The UN’s refugee agency said on Friday it was seeking a much-reduced $7.1 billion to protect stateless people and respond to emergencies in 2027. UNHCR chief Barham Salih warned last month that his agency was being “asked to do the impossible,” overstretched by a huge funding shortfall and near-record population displacements worldwide. articles.title: Saudi innovators take food and water technologies to market
articles.description: RIYADH: Saudi Arabia is investing heavily in water and food research, as startups increasingly turn scientific discoveries into commercial ventures, developing solutions to resource challenges and attracting investor interest. Startups supported by King Abdullah University of Science and Technology have raised approximately $1.4 billion in cumulative funding, reflecting growing investor interest in ventures emerging from the university’s entrepreneurship ecosystem. articles.title: Putin unveils new nuclear submarine
articles.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has unveiled a new nuclear submarine, announcing plans to add five more to the fleet by 2030. The ceremony took place at the Sevmash shipyard, marking the submarine’s induction into the navy.

articles.title: Indonesia, Kuwait agree to strengthen energy security cooperation, boost investment
articles.description: Indonesia and Kuwait have agreed to strengthen energy security cooperation and work closely to boost investment in priority sectors, following a meeting between their foreign ministers in Jakarta. Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir and his Kuwaiti counterpart, Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, held talks under the Joint Commission Meeting mechanism on Thursday, marking the second such meeting since 2019. “Indonesia and Kuwait are committed to further advancing bilateral ties, building on nea

articles.title: Ferrari tension and Verstappen-Russell rivalry shape F1’s Middle East return in Qatar
articles.description: Formula 1 returns to the Middle East, concluding a turbulent season overshadowed by personal conflicts among drivers rather than global politics.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye vow to bolster Kingdom’s security against Houthi attacks
articles.description: RIYADH: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye will accelerate efforts to support the Kingdom’s security amid ongoing Houthi attacks, the three members of the Makkah Alliance for Defense said on Friday. The nations signed the agreement in August and held the second meeting of the Strategic Political and Defense Committee in Islamabad on Friday. articles.title: Bayern injury crisis intensifies with Musiala and Olise joining Harry Kane on injured forward list
articles.description: MUNICH: Jamal Musiala has suffered another muscle injury to acerbate Bayern Munich’s injury crisis in attack, with Michael Olise and Harry Kane already ruled out of Saturday’s visit to Hamburger SV in the Bundesliga. Bayern said Friday their medical department diagnosed Musiala with the injury in his right thigh and that he “will be sidelined until further notice” as a result. articles.title: Russian military flotilla bound for Libya turns around after warship sunk on Nov 22, sources says
articles.description: A Russian convoy heading to Libya turned back after a warship was sunk by Ukrainian drones in Benghazi. This incident highlights Russia’s efforts to safeguard its naval resources.

articles.title: Former Iceland goalkeeper Ingvar Jónsson, who was part of Euro 2016 squad, dies at age 37
articles.description: Ingvar Jónsson, a former Icelandic goalkeeper part of the Euro 2016 squad, has died at the age of 37. His passing was announced by his former club Víkingur, though the cause of death was not disclosed.

articles.title: Yemeni military reports 726 operations against Houthis, claims 121 fighters killed
articles.description: ADEN: Yemen’s Armed Forces say they have carried out 726 operations against Houthi forces in recent hours, claiming that 121 of the group’s commanders and fighters were killed. In a statement, the military spokesperson said the operations were conducted as part of the Dawn of Yemen campaign, targeting Houthi positions, gatherings, reinforcements and fortifications across several fronts. articles.title: US disables ship trying to leave Iran, as Tehran vows to confront blockade
articles.description: The US military disabled a commercial ship attempting to bypass a blockade in Iran. An Iranian official promises to end the blockade and keep the Strait of Hormuz shut.

articles.title: Ex-champion boxer Linares released by US immigration authorities
articles.description: Jorge Linares, a former world boxing champion from Venezuela, has been released by US immigration authorities after being detained for overstaying his visa. He now awaits further legal proceedings.
